Figure 1:Motivation ofDream2Discern.(a)A runtime auditor predicts terminal outcomes from observed prefixes but learns from a limited labeled corpus.(b)Trajectory augmentation seeks broader failure coverage, but collection is costly and editing can invalidate outcome labels (right).
Broader coverage alone does not identify prefixes that the current auditor finds hard to classify.(c)We construct hard latent variants through operator perturbations chosen to increase batch prediction loss, then train on these variants while keeping recorded prefixes and labels unchanged.

Figure 3:Overview ofDream2Discern.①Labeled prefixes.We form a class-balanced batch from recorded success and failure prefixes, keeping their inputs and outcome labels unchanged throughout the training steps.②Dream.With the auditor fixed, we search for shared, bounded, low-rank perturbations to its query and value projection weights that increase batch prediction loss.③Discern.Holding the selected perturbation fixed, we update the LoRA adapters and prediction head to minimize the loss on the resulting hard latent variants.④Runtime auditing.We discard the perturbation and apply a calibrated threshold to each prefix score to predict failure during execution.
